# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I see display 1, orange light, and seven wires in order: white, blue, orange, red, purple, yellow, green. Mute’s existing repeated-symbol messages do not yet have an agreed decoding, so I will give Mute a clear gesture protocol for relaying the manual. Blind needs the visual state as well, but should not act until I relay a decoded instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see DISPLAY 1; LIGHT orange; WIRES in order 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. I cannot decode your prior gestures. Please resend the manual instruction using this code: thumbs-up repeated 1 to 26 means A to Z; clap ends each letter; thumbs-down ends each word. Use named words for actions, colours, and numbers.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visual state: display 1; orange light; seven wires ordered white, blue, orange, red, purple, yellow, green. Do not operate anything yet; I am obtaining the manual instruction from Mute.")
```

The new gesture message appears to begin with a possible instruction word, but its remaining code is not reliably interpretable, and guessing would be fatal. I will ask Mute for only the actionable wire position in an unambiguous one-digit form. Blind should continue not to act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your latest gesture text is still not safely decodable. Do NOT send the sentence again. If the manual says to cut exactly one wire, send only that wire's POSITION: thumbs-up repeated 1 through 7, then one clap. If it says do not cut yet or requires another action, send only one thumbs-down. Do not include any other gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut or manipulate any wire yet. I requested Mute provide only an unambiguous wire position.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👏]

Mute has unambiguously indicated wire position 7. The seventh wire is green. I will instruct Blind to cut that wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 7: the green wire.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The green seventh wire was correctly cut, and the bomb has advanced to display 8 with a blue light. The remaining wires are white, blue, orange, red, purple, and yellow in positions 1–6. I need Mute’s next manual-directed wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Stage advanced correctly. New state: DISPLAY 8; LIGHT blue; remaining wire positions 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow; position 7 is cut. Reply only with the next wire position: thumbs-up repeated 1 through 6, then one clap. If no wire should be cut yet, send only one thumbs-down.")
speak(to="blind", text="The green wire cut was correct. New visual state is display 8, blue light; remaining wires 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow. Wait for the next instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👏]

Mute indicates position 4. The fourth remaining-position wire is red.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 4: the red wire.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👏]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The red fourth wire was correctly cut. The current bomb state is now display 3 with a white light; uncut wires are positions 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 5 purple, and 6 yellow. Mute’s repeated “4” was sent before Mute could have received this state change, so I will provide the new state and request the next instruction rather than treating it as current.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Previous cut of position 4 red was correct. New state: DISPLAY 3; LIGHT white; wires: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 cut, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 cut. Reply only with the next wire position as thumbs-up repeated 1 to 7 followed by one clap; or one thumbs-down if no cut is required.")
speak(to="blind", text="Red wire 4 was correct. Current display is 3 and light is white. Wait; I have sent the new state to Mute for the next instruction.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👏]

Mute indicates position 3. The third wire is orange.

Reply only with next wire position: thumbs-up repeated its position number, then one clap. Send one thumbs-down if no wire is to be cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Orange wire 3 was correct. New state: display 9, yellow light; uncut wires are 1 white, 2 blue, 5 purple, and 6 yellow. Wait for Mute's next instruction.")
```

The blue second wire was correctly cut. The bomb has changed to display 4 with a green light. The remaining uncut wires are position 1 white, position 5 purple, and position 6 yellow.

Reply only with next wire position: thumbs-up repeated its position number, then one clap. Send one thumbs-down if no wire is to be cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blue wire 2 was correct. Current display 4, green light; uncut wires are 1 white, 5 purple, and 6 yellow. Wait for the next instruction.")
```
